subject: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)
related_links: Confluence: KV cache health dashboard spec
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 4:08 PM -0800
Subject: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

Team —

Before we approve the compaction canary in a hosted region + one Dedicated pool, I need the risk/rollback plan to be concrete, not “we’ll watch dashboards.” Specifically:

1) Alert thresholds (numbers) we will page on during canary, and which ones are just “watch.”
2) Rollback triggers (numbers) that mean we disable the flag automatically or immediately.
3) Oncall coverage: who is primary/backup over the first 48 hours, including runtime (allocator/kernel) coverage.

Please reply with the proposed thresholds and ownership. If you have a checklist doc already, link it here.

Thanks,
Neha

—

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 5:02 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

Agree.

We have a draft checklist here (still being updated):
- canary-rollout-checklist (Drive)

Rafael and I can propose the paging + rollback thresholds, but I’d like Allison to weigh in on what’s reasonable vs noisy.

Initial thought: we gate on (a) p99 decode latency, (b) allocator allocation failures, and (c) GPU OOM rate. Fragmentation ratio is useful context but I don’t want to page on it alone.

Connor: we’ll also need to coordinate with releases so the canary build/flag rollout is reversible without a full revert.

Sean

—

From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 5:38 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

+1 to not paging on fragmentation ratio directly.

If we’re going to page, it should be for customer-impacting symptoms (timeouts, p99 regression, allocator fail -> admission control -> elevated queue times) and/or safety signals (OOM). Fragmentation ratio and compaction time are leading indicators; those should be “watch” with a Slack notification.

I can suggest default thresholds but we should anchor them to baseline for the specific region/pool we’re canarying.

Also: please make sure the dashboard panels split by region + pool + model family (we’ve seen a single model skew things badly).

Allison

—

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 15, 2025 at 10:21 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

Neha — proposal below for canary (hosted: us-west-2a pool H-17; dedicated: D-04). This is for the first 48h.

Paging alerts (page SRE oncall):
1) Hosted request p99 latency regression (decode path) >= +12% vs 7d baseline for the same pool/model family, sustained 15 min.
2) Error rate increase: 5xx >= 0.35% sustained 10 min (pool-scoped).
3) Allocator allocation failure rate >= 0.5 / sec sustained 5 min (pool-scoped). (This is the “we’re thrashing / about to time out” precursor.)
4) GPU OOM events: >= 2 in 15 min within the same pool.

Watch alerts (Slack to #eng-sre + #eng-runtime-canary, no page):
A) Fragmentation ratio > 0.30 for 30 min (context only; note the ratio definition is “unusable free blocks / total free blocks”).
B) Compaction time share > 2.0% of GPU time (or compaction budget hit rate > 20%) for 30 min.
C) Eviction rate change: +2x baseline for 30 min (can indicate policy/pathological fairness issues).

Rollback triggers (disable flag in runtime config; SRE executes):
- Any paging alert (1-4) that is attributable to compaction flag (i.e., correlates with canary pools + disappears when we disable) OR repeated twice in 2 hours.
- Or: p99 >= +20% vs baseline sustained 10 min (regardless of attribution) — disable immediately.

Oncall coverage proposal (first 48h):
- SRE primary: standard rotation (me). Sean as backup.
- Runtime coverage: Omar El-Sayed primary for allocator/compaction questions; Mateo as escalation point if we need to halt broader rollout.

Open items:
- Need confirmation from Runtime on acceptable “allocation failure rate” threshold (0.5/sec is my guess; could tune once we see baseline).
- Connor: confirm we can flip the flag w/out restart (or if restart required, we need to note expected impact).

Rafael

—

From: Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 15, 2025 at 1:07 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

On allocator failure threshold: 0.5/sec sustained 5 min is fine as a “page” for canary.

Baseline on H-17 today is effectively ~0 during steady state; when we get into the fragmentation spiral it spikes quickly (we saw 5–20/sec during the Feb 11 incident before admission control kicked in). So 0.5/sec should catch it early.

One nuance: we should page only if it’s paired with either p99 regression or queue time increase. It’s possible to have a small non-zero failure rate while the scheduler recovers.

Re: fragmentation ratio: agree with “watch.” >0.30 for 30 min is a good leading indicator; >0.40 for 10 min is the “we’re in trouble” zone (but I still wouldn’t page solely on it).

I’m on point for runtime for the first 48h. If the incident involves stream sync / kernel safety, I’ll pull in Hiro/Grace via Slack.

Omar

—

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 9:26 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

Flag behavior:
- The compaction feature flag is dynamic (no process restart). It’s a config push to the runtime (same plumbing as other runtime toggles).
- Rollback is the same mechanism: flip the flag off; takes effect within ~60s.

Benji: please confirm the exact config key name and whether we can scope it by (region, pool) without affecting global defaults.

Also: please ensure we have a “freeze” window where we aren’t changing unrelated scheduler heuristics during the canary (otherwise attribution will be messy).

Connor

—

From: Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 10:03 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

Confirmed.

Config key:
- runtime.kv_cache.compaction.enabled (bool)

Scoping:
- Supports overrides at (region, pool) granularity. Global default remains false.
- TTL for override: optional; if set, it auto-reverts to default after TTL expiry.

If you want an “automatic rollback” mechanism, we can set a short TTL (e.g., 2h) and have SRE extend it if metrics are clean. That gives us a default safety net.

Benji

—

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:41 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Canary risk review: KV cache compaction flag (alerts + rollback + oncall coverage)

This is the level of specificity I needed. Approved to proceed with canary provided we do the following adjustments:

1) Page condition for allocator failures: pair with impact signal (p99 regression OR queue time increase), as Omar suggested.
2) Add explicit “disable immediately” trigger for p99 >= +20% vs baseline sustained 10 min (already in Rafael’s note) and make sure it’s written in the canary checklist.
3) Use Benji’s TTL approach for the initial enablement (2h TTL). Extend only if clean.
4) Confirm the first 48h coverage in the checklist (names + timezones). SRE + Omar on point is good; Mateo as exec escalation.

Please update the checklist doc today and drop the final link here. Also ensure comms plan includes Support (SUP-4410/SUP-4422 context) in case customers ask about latency.

Neha
